title: EXP-013 — Immediate Form Variable Definition Retention Across One Ordinary Save
objective: Using one new User-scope classic BuildFromScratch Form, establish or confirm a live Mongoose session before mutation, prove the new target is absent, create exactly one Form variable named FX_ImmediateSaveRetentionVar with Global=False, Persistent=True, and Value=Seed-Save-C, record every visible definition field, perform exactly one ordinary Designer Save, and immediately verify whether the same design-time definition remains unchanged after Save. The experiment ends after the immediate post-Save comparison and does not test Form close/reopen, runtime value persistence, cache behavior, session replacement, or storage provenance.

in_scope: Before any Mongoose artifact mutation, confirm or establish a supported live Mongoose/Web Client session without exposing credential values.
Prove the session is live with an observable server-backed check and confirm editing scope is User.
Prove FX_FormVariableLab03 is absent exact and case-insensitive in the live Select Form inventory before mutation.
Create exactly one new User-scope classic BuildFromScratch Form named FX_FormVariableLab03 using the verified basic-form recipe with Save Template unchecked.
Open Details > Variables and create exactly one Form variable named FX_ImmediateSaveRetentionVar.
Set Global=False, Persistent=True, and design-time Value=Seed-Save-C.
Record every visible variable-definition field before Save as the comparison baseline.
Perform exactly one ordinary Designer Save.
Immediately re-read Details > Variables and compare every recorded visible definition field against the pre-Save baseline.
Capture screenshots and read-only diagnostics under evidence/EXP-013/ and update only the EXP-013 experiment record plus its evidence directory.

Prefer completing the semantic mutation through immediate post-Save verification in one bounded worker task after preflight so the experiment tests Save retention rather than cross-turn idle/session behavior.
out_of_scope: Replaying, repairing, changing, or promoting EXP-004, EXP-011, or EXP-012.
Treating EXP-013 as a replay of EXP-012.
Closing or reopening FX_FormVariableLab03 after Save.
Testing whether the variable definition survives Form-tab close/reopen, a new Designer client, logout/login, session replacement, cache unload, or any other lifecycle boundary.
Executing Form logic to read, initialize, mutate, or otherwise test the runtime value of the variable.
Testing Persistent=False or creating a comparison variable.
Using Regenerate Form or any second save mechanism.
Unload All Global Form Objects, deliberate IDO metadata unloading, cache-clearing experiments, or User Preferences.
Caption, Description, component, collection, binding, validator, event handler, script, data-source, IDO-definition, localized-String, portal, Runtime Builder, or FormSync experiments.
Site, Group, or Vendor Default editing scope.
Modification of any existing FX_ artifact.
Creation or modification of reusable recipes, AGENTS.md, environment files, or other experiment records.
Physical Forms-database provenance, direct database inspection or mutation, undocumented APIs, or internal session manipulation.
Any claim that immediate post-Save retention proves durable database storage, close/reopen persistence, cache eviction, runtime value persistence, or storage provenance.

acceptance_checks.description: Before any Mongoose artifact mutation, evidence proves either the inherited session was already live or the supported session-establishment flow was completed; afterward a server-backed liveness check succeeds, editing scope is User, and FX_FormVariableLab03 is absent exact and case-insensitive in the live inventory.

Exactly one new User-scope classic BuildFromScratch Form named FX_FormVariableLab03 exists after creation through the verified basic-form recipe with Save Template unchecked; live inventory evidence proves exactly one case-insensitive target.

Before Save, Details > Variables visibly contains exactly one experiment-created variable named FX_ImmediateSaveRetentionVar with Global=False, Persistent=True, Value=Seed-Save-C where Value is exposed, and every visible definition field is recorded as the comparison baseline.
Exactly one ordinary Designer Save is performed after variable creation, no Regenerate Form or second Save occurs, and evidence proves the Designer returns to a clean state.
Immediately after the single ordinary Save, Details > Variables contains exactly one FX_ImmediateSaveRetentionVar and every recorded visible design-time definition field equals the AC-3 baseline.
Evidence and the experiment record prove there was no Form close/reopen, explicit unload/cache-clear, User Preferences action, runtime Form execution, or second save mechanism during the experiment.

Evidence and the record prove that any session-establishment action occurred only before the first Mongoose artifact mutation; after FX_FormVariableLab03 creation began, no login, Sign In/OK, deliberate reauthentication, logout, browser restart, or deliberate session replacement occurred.

The experiment record classifies only the observed immediate design-time definition retention or non-retention across one ordinary Save and explicitly makes no close/reopen persistence, runtime-value-persistence, cache, database-durability, or storage-provenance claim.

Final repository/worktree audit proves experiment-attributable changes are confined to the EXP-013 record and evidence/EXP-013/, with no recipe, AGENTS.md, environment, other experiment, existing FX_ artifact, or non-FX_ artifact modified.

notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261003-025358-Ts8m. Rationale: EXP-012 established the pre-Save variable-definition workflow but was blocked before the first Save because the Mongoose session expired across multiple coordinator/worker boundaries. The smallest next learning step is not to retry EXP-012's close/reopen persistence objective, but to isolate the first unresolved semantic boundary: whether one Global=False, Persistent=True Form-variable definition survives exactly one ordinary Designer Save. This is a narrower, distinct experiment with no close/reopen lifecycle test. It should execute the semantic sequence in one bounded worker task after a live-session preflight, minimizing unrelated idle-time exposure while preserving the rule that session establishment is allowed only before mutation. EXP-004's older failures remain relevant historical evidence, but EXP-013 uses the now-observed current Variables UI workflow and records the exact current 2026.09.08 design-time definition before and immediately after Save rather than testing runtime values or Regenerate.
